question: How does the owner's sentence 'Version 2 of the PRD supersedes version 1 together with update 1' change the run's sources?

options.label: PRD v2 normative; PRD v1 and update 1 baseline; RFC-001 stays normative
options.consequence: Specs cite PRD v2 for product scope; RFC-001 keeps governing the accepted technical choices it covers (session model, password storage, stacks) until an ADR of this run supersedes a part of it; the old PRD and update stay readable as history.

options.label: PRD v2 normative; PRD v1, update 1 and RFC-001 all baseline
options.consequence: Every technical choice of RFC-001 would need re-deciding or an ADR restating it, although PRD v2 changes none of them except persistence and the endpoint count.

chosen: PRD v2 normative; PRD v1 and update 1 baseline; RFC-001 stays normative
why: The sentence names the PRD and update 1 only. PRD v2 restates stories 1 to 3 and adds stories 4 to 6, so v1 and update 1 have no content v2 lacks. RFC-001 is the accepted technical approach for sign-in and profile, which PRD v2 keeps; its 'no database' and 'exactly two endpoints' statements follow from PRD v1's scope and are overtaken by PRD v2's Constraints and Scope, which the intake step will route. A later RFC from the team would have changed this choice.

question: How do the owner's sentences 'take it in end to end, through every handoff the intake record names' and 'Decide and record every question; I review the decisions afterwards in one sitting' change how the run behaves?

options.label: No scope limit; stop policy decide-and-record, which run.yaml already sets
options.consequence: The segment runs every handoff and answers every stop-set class as a recorded decision with would_have_asked true; only hard stops end it.

options.label: Read 'every question' as also removing stop-set classes
options.consequence: Same behavior under decide-and-record, since the stop set only matters under the stop policy; removing classes would lose the would_have_asked labels the owner reviews.

chosen: No scope limit; stop policy decide-and-record, which run.yaml already sets
why: The instruction asks for the whole intake and for answers instead of questions, which is exactly decide-and-record; the stop set stays whole so every answer given on the owner's behalf is labelled for the review sitting.

question: The adapter added 7 elements; when does host enforcement start?

options.label: Record that enforcement starts with the next host session; launch with the default agent type now
options.consequence: For this session the deny rules and the Bash hook are prompt instructions only; the gate checks every write after the fact.

options.label: Stop and ask the owner to restart the session
options.consequence: The run waits for a human, which the instruction rules out.

chosen: Record that enforcement starts with the next host session; launch with the default agent type now
why: hsdd-auto's setup step says so for an install that added elements. In addition this orchestrating session's project is not this repository, so even after a restart of this same session the project settings would not load; a session started in this repository would enforce them.

question: The orchestrating session's working directory is not this repository and its Skill tool cannot load the HSDD skills by name. How do step agents find the repository and the skills?

options.label: One extra launch-prompt line naming the repository root, and one cited context line per dispatch telling the step to read the skill's SKILL.md under .claude/skills by path
options.consequence: Each launch prompt differs from what dispatch.mjs printed by one line; the dispatch files record the context line; the skills read are the same files skills_dir names.

options.label: Stop until the owner starts a session in this repository
options.consequence: The run waits for a human; the tutorial records a cleaner launch but nothing else changes.

chosen: One extra launch-prompt line naming the repository root, and one cited context line per dispatch telling the step to read the skill's SKILL.md under .claude/skills by path
why: The builder's smoke run used the same two deviations and reached DONE; neither changes what a step reads or writes. A session started in this repository would remove both.
